findings.claim: Section 3 still defines the practical as 'the coding part (Part 2) of collections-module-check, unchanged', and line 64 keeps that legacy blueprint 'unchanged ... as the source of the practical'. That blueprint's public instructions and item split put Part 2 at 30 minutes (15 MCQ minutes + 30 coding minutes = 45). So the file still points readers to a 30-minute practical record, while section 7 (line 194, line 197) now states a 90-minute practical whose 'duration is unchanged'. Line 196 explains only that the 45-minute total is the calendar block. It does not say that the 30-minute Part 2 timing is superseded. Line 65 likewise still calls the 15-item/15-minute Part 1 'the course's existing planned MCQ component', while section 7 records the accepted former MCQ as 40 minutes. The practical record has not been reconciled to 90 minutes everywhere in the file.
findings.recommendation: In section 3 (lines 56, 64-65) and the taxonomy row at line 247, state that the practical is sourced from the legacy blueprint's coding tasks but runs 90 minutes per the accepted time plan. Say that the legacy blueprint's 15/30 split is the superseded F28 calendar-block plan. Name the accepted 40-minute MCQ as the component the 60-minute final MCQ replaces. Do not edit the legacy blueprint in this record.

findings.claim: The placement conflict is understated. It presents the problem as only 'neither final fits the 45-minute block' and asks the owner to place 150 minutes 'inside the course's F25 to F28 envelope', as if free time exists there. The intake's Day-block allocation (intake.md lines 163-170) already fills F25 116, F26 120, F27 114 and F28 120 minutes, which is 470 of 480. Only 45 of those minutes are assessment time. Placing 150 assessment minutes needs 105 more minutes when only 10 are unallocated. The 465/480 figure (line 197) holds only under the time plan's allocation of 225 content, 2 x 30 labs and 2 x 15 mastery. It does not hold under the intake's calendar allocation, which plans labs of 47 and 45 minutes (intake.md lines 121-122) against the plan's 30-minute lab cap and has no mastery-check minutes. The genuine conflict is that the calendar days as allocated cannot hold the accepted finals. It is not only a block-size mismatch.
findings.recommendation: Restate the conflict as follows. Under the intake's Day-block allocation, F25-F28 have 10 unallocated minutes against 105 extra assessment minutes, plus the lab-cap gap (92 planned vs 60 accepted). Placing the separate 90- and 60-minute sittings inside 480 minutes therefore requires the course owner to replace or re-plan existing day blocks to match the accepted plan's allocation. Do not cut coverage, repurpose the module-check block or add hours. Mirror this in the section 9 open decision (line 234).
